title: Calibration-covariance provenance and shared-nuisance double-count tribunal
hypothesis: A deterministic synthetic calibration docket can expose omitted covariance and double-counted shared nuisance uncertainty while preserving units and a hard zero-real-row lock.
null_or_failure: Shared calibration uncertainty is counted as independent, covariance origin is absent, units disagree, the covariance matrix is asymmetric or non-positive-semidefinite without quarantine, thresholds are tuned after outputs, or synthetic propagation becomes a real-data GMUT likelihood claim.
test_falsifier_or_gate: Run independent, shared-nuisance, omitted-covariance, double-counted, asymmetric, non-positive-semidefinite, unit-mismatch, and post-hoc-threshold fixtures; require expected rejection while real rows, likelihoods, fits, and independent reviews remain zero.
rollback_or_recovery: Retain the failed covariance fixture, restore its declared nuisance graph and units, freeze calibration handling before future data access, and require a separately preregistered real-data analysis for promotion.
boundary: Calibration fixtures are synthetic with zero real rows, likelihoods, fits, or independent statistical reviews.
